testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What happens when cargo is loaded with a high center of gravity?

options.text: It increases the risk of the vehicle rolling over.
It increases the chance that items will fall down.
It makes unloading the cargo harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of the vehicle rolling over.
questions.explanation: Cargo loaded with a high center of gravity makes the vehicle more likely to tip over. Always load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: What is true about oversized loads?

options.text: They can never be transported by a truck.
They should only be transported during the day.
They need proper permits to follow state and local laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need proper permits to follow state and local laws.
questions.explanation: Special permits are required for loads that are oversized, over-length, or overweight.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid using your mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only at the front and right side of your vehicle.
Look at the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You need to know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly on both sides while driving.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need to stay alert?

options.text: Six to seven hours
Seven to eight hours
Eight to nine hours
Four to five hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Eight to nine hours
questions.explanation: Getting proper rest is essential for safe driving. Most adults need eight to nine hours of sleep per night to stay alert.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
When you have a passenger
When you are carrying a heavy load

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roads are wet, snowy, or icy
questions.explanation: A retarder helps slow your vehicle and reduces the need for braking. But it can cause wheels to skid on slippery roads. Turn it off when roads are wet, snowy, or icy.

questions.question: How often should you inspect your cargo during a trip?

options.text: Only before you start driving
At the end of each day
Every time you take a break

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you take a break
questions.explanation: Check your cargo and how it is secured every time you take a break. Inspect it at least every 150 miles.

questions.question: What is the safest speed to drive in heavy traffic?

options.text: The posted speed limit
The speed of the surrounding traffic
Much slower than the surrounding traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the surrounding traffic
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, match the speed of other vehicles. Vehicles traveling at the same speed in the same direction are less likely to crash. However, do not exceed the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What happens if your engine does not have enough oil?

options.text: The vehicle will have trouble stopping.
The vehicle will make quick, jerking movements while driving.
The engine can be damaged quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be damaged quickly.
questions.explanation: Your engine must have enough oil to function properly. An engine can be destroyed rapidly without adequate oil.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play makes steering difficult?

options.text: More than 10 degrees
More than 25 degrees
More than 50 degrees

questions.correctAnswerText: More than 10 degrees
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should have no more than 10 degrees of play. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. More play than this makes steering difficult.

questions.question: What do you need to transport hazardous materials that require placards?

options.text: Permission from local law enforcement
A hazardous materials endorsement
Permission to transport at night only

questions.correctAnswerText: A hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a hazardous materials endorsement to transport materials that require placards.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: Stop cargo from moving during transport.
Stop cargo from being loaded too high.
Stop cargo from being unloaded too quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from moving during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed in front, behind, and/or on the sides of cargo to keep it from sliding when the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It is not a concern.
It only happens when people do something physical while driving.
It can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
It is acceptable on empty roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving: set radio stations before driving, plan your route ahead of time, avoid difficult conversations, adjust mirrors before leaving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: Which tire condition is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Tires of different sizes
Tires with cracks
Tires from different manufacturers

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires from different manufacturers
questions.explanation: Always inspect your tires before a trip. Tire sizes must match, and tires must not have cuts, cracks, or any other damage.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only mechanics should use them.
Only use them when it is wet outside.
Completely drain the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Completely drain the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from air brake system tanks. Always drain the tank completely.

questions.question: What should you do shortly after changing a tire?

options.text: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
Repair the brakes.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: What must interstate carriers display on both sides of a CMV?

options.text: USDOT number
Truck model number
Destination

questions.correctAnswerText: USDOT number
questions.explanation: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations require carriers to display the USDOT number on both sides of each CMV in their fleet.

questions.question: What is a trailer brake hand valve used for?

options.text: Add fuel to the truck.
Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
Check the engine oil level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: If a tractor-trailer has a trailer brake hand valve, it can be used to stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.question: Which item is not required safety equipment?

options.text: A fire extinguisher
A liquid burning flare
An axe

questions.correctAnswerText: An axe
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and at least one properly charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.
Drink some coffee.
Drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to reach your destination while tired—it is dangerous. Caffeine is not a safe solution.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?

options.text: Make eye contact.
Try to stay in their way.
Ignore their hand gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their hand gestures.
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact—it may make them more angry. Ignore any hand gestures they make.

questions.question: What makes up the emergency brake system?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three types of brakes: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Drive faster.
Make hand gestures at other drivers.
Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers have good reasons for their actions.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, assume other drivers have valid reasons for what they do. Do not take their actions personally.

questions.question: What should you do during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Follow the same steps in the same order every time.
Complete it as quickly as possible.
Ignore small mechanical problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the same steps in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Use the same process every time you do a pre-trip inspection. This helps you remember all the important steps and ensures nothing gets missed.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch the road ahead of you?

options.text: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
It distracts you from driving.
It is only important in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always look ahead at the road. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail going downhill?

options.text: Drive onto an escape ramp.
Let the vehicle slow down by itself.
Use rumble strips to slow the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive onto an escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, find an escape ramp to stop your vehicle. If no escape ramp is available, look for a flat area or uphill road to slow down.

questions.question: How does a truck's weight affect stopping distance?

options.text: It has no impact on stopping distance.
It is a major factor in stopping distance.
The cargo type matters more than weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major factor in stopping distance.
questions.explanation: Weight is very important for stopping distance. Heavier vehicles need more braking power to stop completely.

questions.question: Is it a good idea to use a helper when backing up a large vehicle?

options.text: Yes, it is encouraged.
No, it is discouraged.
No, it is illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is encouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing up a large vehicle is dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind you. Using a helper to watch your blind spots is encouraged whenever possible.

questions.question: How should you press the brake pedal when stopping?

options.text: Press it down slowly.
Press it down quickly.
Press it down in short bursts, not continuously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down slowly.
questions.explanation: When stopping, press the brake pedal down slowly and gradually.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts indicate?

options.text: It has rained recently.
The nuts may be loose.
The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts may be loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean they are loose. Check the tightness of the nuts if you see rust.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop your vehicle within:

options.text: 10 feet of your vehicle.
100 feet of your vehicle.
The distance you can see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must be able to stop within the area of road you can see. Slow down when visibility is reduced.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill:

options.text: Use the air brakes.
Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
Downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep hills, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only to help, not as your main way to slow down.

questions.question: A cargo van is:

options.text: Usually the same height whether it is empty or loaded.
Usually taller when carrying a heavy load than a light load.
Usually shorter when carrying a heavy load than a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually shorter when carrying a heavy load than a light load.
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower. A vehicle is taller when it carries a light load than when it carries a heavy load. If your vehicle fits under a bridge when full, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirrors.
Use both side mirrors.
Never use a helper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Backing a truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both mirrors often when backing. Use a helper when you can.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car:

options.text: You must tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation in any vehicle. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: Texting while driving should:

options.text: Only be done on straight roads.
Only be done in curves.
Not be done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not be done.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is a dangerous distraction. It is never allowed when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What do both parts of a dual air brake system share?

options.text: Hoses
An air compressor
Air tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the air compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Keep cargo in a large box.
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
Stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: The only way to become sober after drinking alcohol is to:

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Exercise.
Wait.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers or coffee will not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to let your body process the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: A bridge formula:

options.text: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
Allows more weight for trucks.
Is not important for drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows less weight per axle when axles are close together.
questions.explanation: Bridge formulas set the maximum weight allowed on axles. Axles that are close together have lower weight limits.

questions.question: Escape ramps are used to:

options.text: Only by cars, not trucks.
Leave the highway and enter a two-lane road.
Stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop runaway vehicles on steep downhills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep hills to safely stop vehicles that lose their brakes. They are filled with loose, soft material and sometimes slope upward.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Watch the gauges
Use your senses
Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip
questions.explanation: You should check your vehicle regularly during a trip. Look at the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses and watch for any early signs of trouble.

questions.question: When stopping, you should press the brake pedal by:

options.text: Pushing down gradually
Pushing down quickly
Pulling up gradually

questions.correctAnswerText: Pushing down gradually
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually when stopping. This helps you keep full control of your vehicle.

questions.question: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move, you can:

options.text: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal
Put the vehicle in second gear
Use the parking brake when stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal
questions.explanation: Partly engage the clutch before removing your foot from the brake pedal. This prevents your vehicle from rolling backward.

questions.question: A DUI conviction will suspend your license for a minimum of:

options.text: 30 days
Six months
One year

questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: A first DUI conviction suspends your license for at least one year. A second conviction results in a lifetime suspension.

questions.question: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Stay on
Flicker occasionally
Turn off immediately

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off immediately
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and ABS should turn off right away.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used with caution because:

options.text: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and could catch fire
Other drivers may not see flares on sunny days
Flares are expensive

questions.correctAnswerText: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and could catch fire
questions.explanation: Using flares near spilled fuel can cause vehicle fires. Use flares carefully.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Should never be done the same way twice in a row
Should always be done in the same order
Do not need to be done if the vehicle seems fine

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be done in the same order
questions.explanation: Do your vehicle inspection in the same order every time. This makes it easier to learn and helps you remember every step.

questions.question: Which of the following convictions disqualifies someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Arson
Speeding
Littering

questions.correctAnswerText: Arson
questions.explanation: A felony conviction for arson disqualifies you from getting, renewing, or transferring a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: You should test the low pressure warning signal by:

options.text: Starting the engine and applying the trailer hand brake
Pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly
Removing wheel chocks and disengaging the parking brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly
questions.explanation: After the system charges, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air and the warning should activate when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Cargo inside a trailer:

options.text: Does not need to be secured
Should be stacked no more than three feet high
Should be secured to prevent movement

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be secured to prevent movement
questions.explanation: Cargo in a trailer must be secured so it does not shift while the vehicle is moving.
